answer: The promoted AI order slot never becomes the order ring's +148h/+14Ch. 00811D10 copies only the record's +00h..+3Fh across the index flip, so the published triple stays at unit+0A98h+54h*index, which is the address every reader of it computes; all three readers are in the AI segment and 009D8CE0 reads two different units' triples. The ring's throttle and rudder are written only by 00813020's step toward slot[readCursor], by the two immediate setters, by the ring constructor and by the unit+61h block inlined at 008266CE..0082674C, and slot[writeCursor] is filled only by 0080DAD0 whose one caller 00816A40 has three HUD callers. The slot is the ship AI's published navigation state, not a command to the unit.

verification.note: Rows under undefined_region_steps use site/callee instead of address/native because no Ghidra function contains those call sites. The three ranges are listed under no_ghidra_function in docs/UNIT_AI_ORDER_SLOT_READER.md and docs/UNIT_MANUAL_AUTOPILOT.md; all three are unreferenced out-of-line copies, so defining them is optional.

run.stand_in: the slot-to-rudder hop. The scan shows no native reader of slot +40h/+44h/+48h on the unit's motion path, so the probe closes the loop with a proportional law over the -/+ pi/4 window 00811960 clamps to. The run is evidence about the published triple and about the reconstructed motion, not about the shipped steering law.
